text:
Maya: quick design sync — want to lock down compact preview for eval suites before next week's release. main concerns: score summary density, CTA placement for bulk actions, and keyboard/aria flows. sharing mocks.
Jon: thanks — looked through Figma. two quick things: 1) compact rows feel fine but score badges collapse confusingly at <320px, 2) bulk approve CTA competes with export button.
Priya: from research, users expect a clear primary action per row (approve/reject) and a global bulk action. they repeatedly reached for the row-level affordance when the primary control was global.
Alex: implementation note — current table uses CSS grid + `display: none` for mobile. switching to `aria-hidden` + visually-hidden toggle will be more a11y-friendly. will add keyboard trap tests.
Sam: accessibility nits: contrast for the score badge (green-on-white) fails AA at small sizes; also the bulk banner needs `role="region"` + `aria-label` so screen readers announce it. suggest `aria-live="polite"` on status updates.
Maya: proposed copy for the banner and CTA — please react or suggest edits:```banner: "Approve selected prompt results (affects X tests)" primary CTA: "Approve X" secondary: "Export CSV" helper text: "You can undo bulk approvals in Activity"```
Jon: copy tweak — make primary verb more action-oriented: "Approve selected" (no X in CTA). keep counts in helper text only. :+1: for moving export to kebab menu.
Priya: agree with Jon. also add an informational tooltip on hover: "Approving marks these prompts as passed for the current run" — users asked for that in studies.
Alex: technical: to keep layout consistent we can show a condensed badge like `45/60` instead of percentage on small widths. easier layout-wise and still informative.
Sam: keyboard flow: when toggling select-all, focus should remain on the banner CTA not jump. propose `focus()` on the CTA with `preventScroll: true`. also ensure `aria-pressed` state on the bulk toggle.
Maya: design ask for Jon — can we try a stacked banner variant (count above, CTAs below) vs inline (count left, CTAs right)? which scales better?
Jon: stacked wins for small screens, inline for >= 880px. will upload both variants to the spec with annotated breakpoints.
Alex: we'll need a small E2E to assert that `aria-live` fires and keyboard focus stays. adding a CI job — CI-bot will run a11y smoke after deploy.
CI-bot: queued job: `a11y-smoke/eval-compact-preview` (reacts :white_check_mark:)
Priya: one more microcopy note — helper text should mention undo window: "You can undo bulk approvals for 48 hours" — was helpful in tests.
Maya: love that. final checklist: - Jon upload stacked/inline variants - Alex add `aria-live` + focus handling + E2E - Sam verify contrast and `aria-*` attributes - Priya finalize tooltip + undo copy - I'll schedule a quick sign-off at Tue design review.
Jon: will do. posting new frames in ~30m. :eyes:
Alex: started branch `feat/compact-preview-a11y` and will PR once CI passes.
Sam: I'll run a quick VoiceOver pass when frames are up.
Maya: thanks team — short follow-ups in thread please. :)
